The air around me shimmered with colors and patterns that danced like rainbows across the walls. Each moment seemed to be painted with layers of detail until the mind lost itself in the beauty.

"It flew by quicker than I could comprehend," I thought to myself, but what I truly saw were the faces surrounding me - all those who sought comfort in these machines designed for endless entertainment. Each person looked at me, not out of curiosity or understanding, but solely because they wanted something different from their own lives.

One glance into every room revealed a monotony that would leave anyone feeling trapped beneath its harsh glare. The conversations were forced, filled with banality more fitting for a kindergarten class than an adult's thoughts. They spoke about jobs they couldn't keep, homes they didn't have, families they couldn’t share; their lives reduced down to a single topic each day.

I watched the woman in front of me sip her cold coffee, the way she bit her lip when no one laughed at her jokes, her gaze wandering past me towards someone else’s conversation. In another corner, there sat an old man holding hands with his young grandson, though he smiled none too often. Their laughter was soft and genuine, but here, amidst all the bustling, nothing quite matched the essence.

Eventually, fatigue crept over me as memories started playing back, slowly pulling apart each façade I believed I was seeing through. I walked further away from them, watching as each person turned back to their screens, ready once more to hide within the cocoon of a virtual world where nothing needed changing.
